note: Both sets cover the same four claims (generator-torque inverse relation, Eq. 7-6, Eq. 7-7, and the PID law) with correct conditions and supporting quotes. The key difference is the PID control law: Set A's derivative term drops the time-derivative dot on ΔΩ̇ (reading K_D·N_Gear·ΔΩ instead of K_D·N_Gear·ΔΩ̇), which misstates the control law, while Set B reproduces it correctly. Set B's remaining formulas and conditions match the page, so it is the more faithful set.
remarks: Set B's quotes contain garbled LaTeX fragments (e.g. 'rac{P_0}', tab characters where 'theta' should be), apparently inherited from the text layer rather than a misreading; the underlying expressions are still correct. Both sets omit the first-order Taylor expansions (Eqs. 7-8 and 7-9), which are arguably secondary to the four extracted claims.
